Samir (Sales): quick presales question — prospect wants EU-only data residency for PII. They're ok with cross-border control plane calls but want inference and logs to stay in EU. also asking which subprocessors are actually in-region and whether routing failover to APAC would break compliance. any quick answers?
Ashley (Solutions Eng): short answer: we can pin tenant traffic to EU regions for inference and KV caching. control plane calls (billing/console) may touch US by default unless they sign the Private contract or we enable EU-only control plane.
Samir (Sales): they'd prefer hosted, not private, if we can prove in-region subprocessors and a fallback policy that doesn't leave data outside EU for inference.
Maria (Ops): note: some observability and alerting (3rd-party metrics) go through vendor endpoints with US egress. we can toggle a limited observability stack for the customer (EU-only or agent-forwarding) but it changes how we do incident snapshots.
Samir (Sales): ok — can you list the subprocessors we use in EU and which ones have EU-only endpoints? they need names + certs for the security questionnaire.
Ashley (Solutions Eng): current EU subprocessors: AWS (eu-west-1) for compute/storage, Fastly (EU POPs) for edge, and Vault-as-a-Service (key-management) — we offer KMS routing to a EU KMS. Datadog is used for some hosted metrics but we can opt them out; we also have an EU-only metrics pipeline (self-hosted) as an alternative. I can attach the cert list.
Samir (Sales): great — what about routing failover? they want automatic failover to APAC only for DR, but must guarantee no primary inference request routes to US.
Pete (NetOps): routing model is sticky-by-tenant with failover policy. default: route to nearest healthy EU pool. if an entire EU pool is down, failover options are: 1) block requests (strict residency), 2) failover to another EU pool in a different AZ/region, 3) failover to APAC/NA (not allowed here). we can configure tenant policy to option 1 or 2.
Samir (Sales): can option 2 always be satisfied? e.g., if EU capacity exhausted during huge traffic spike, will we block or route out of EU?
Maria (Ops): capacity constraints: Dedicated customers get guaranteed commit. Hosted customers: we do best-effort; for strict EU-only we can add a fallback hold (reject) + a quota uplift option for burst capacity. for pricing that typically means a regional reservation add-on.
Samir (Sales): pricing ask — give me a ballpark delta for EU-only residency and strict failover=no-route.
Ashley (Solutions Eng): ballpark: residency add-on ~€2,000/mo for EU-only routing + regional standby capacity pricing depends on expected RPS (we usually quote a small reserved pool for €1,000–€5,000/mo). egress is billed separately: typical $0.01–$0.05/GB depending on carrier. BYOK / KMS routing one-time setup €1,500. (these are ballparks; ops/legal to confirm).
Amy (Legal): for the security questionnaire we'll need: signed subprocessors addendum, DPA addendum listing EU subprocessors, and confirmation of server-side key residency if BYOK requested. If they require SOC2 evidence for subprocessors, provide cert URLs.
Samir (Sales): perfect — customer also asked whether we can provide logs proving inference execution stayed in EU for a sample period (for audit).
Maria (Ops): we have data-path logs. we can produce a 7-day egress log showing origin/destination datacenter IDs and ASNs. that's delivered as CSV + a short attestation. note: redaction needed for PII.
Pete (NetOps): config snippet for tenant pinning (internal):
```
routing: 
  default_policy: eu-only
  failover: reject_on_eu_loss
  pinned_region: eu-west-1
```
This enforces reject-on-failover. Expect +50–200ms tail latency in cross-region health checks; no data leaves EU.
Samir (Sales): great. deploy-bot — any capacity windows next week if we need to enable a reserved pool for their POC?
deploy-bot: Deploy window available: Wed 09:00-11:00 UTC next week. Reservation required 48h prior. :white_check_mark:
Samir (Sales): next steps I'll: 1) send subprocessors list + cert links, 2) include Maria's sample log offer, 3) confirm rough pricing and include BYOK setup. Can Ashley/Amy confirm the documents before I share?
Ashley (Solutions Eng): I'll attach cert URLs and the EU-only operations runbook by EOD.
Amy (Legal): I can review the DPA/addendum draft tomorrow and flag anything missing.
Maria (Ops): I'll prepare the sample 7-day egress log template and note redaction instructions.
Samir (Sales): thanks all — I'll schedule the intro call with the customer for Wed 10:00 UTC and share the materials beforehand. :thumbsup:
